metadata.author: omorros

description:
## 🔗 Related Issue                                                                                                   
  Closes #3643
                                                                                                                        
  ## 📝 Summary
  Replaced manual header forwarding loops in the three direct proxy functions (`_proxy_list_tools_to_gateway`,
  `_proxy_list_resources_to_gateway`, `_proxy_read_resource_to_gateway`) with calls to                                    `compute_passthrough_headers_cached()`, fixing the silently dropped `X-Upstream-Authorization → Authorization` rename
  and restoring global passthrough header config support on all direct proxy operations.                                
  
  ---

  ## 🏷️ Type of Change
  - [x] Bug fix
  - [ ] Feature / Enhancement
  - [ ] Documentation
  - [ ] Refactor
  - [ ] Chore (deps, CI, tooling)
  - [ ] Other (describe below)
                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                        
  ## 🧪 Verification

  | Check                     | Command         | Status |
  |---------------------------|-----------------|--------|
  | Lint suite                | `make lint`     | ✅     |
  | Unit tests                | `make test`     | ✅     |
  | Coverage ≥ 80%            | `make coverage` | ✅     |                                                                 
  ---                                                                                                                   
  
  ## ✅ Checklist
  - [x] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`)
  - [x] Tests added/updated for changes
  - [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)                                                                             
  - [x] No secrets or credentials committed
                                                                                                                        
  ---

  ## 📓 Notes (optional)
  The `db` parameter was added as optional (`None` default) to the three proxy functions to avoid breaking any other
  callers. All three call sites already operate inside `async with get_db() as db:` blocks, so passing `db` required no   structural changes. 350 transport tests and 75 passthrough header utility tests pass.

reviews.author: marekdano
reviews.body:
@omorros - thanks for the PR!

### Overall Assessment: Positive — fixes a real security gap

The PR correctly replaces ad-hoc manual header forwarding with the shared `compute_passthrough_headers_cached()` utility, which provides proper sanitization and the `X-Upstream-Authorization → Authorization` rename. This is a clear improvement.

This is a security improvement:

The new code passes `gateway_auth_type` which enables the check that blocks client `Authorization` passthrough when the gateway itself uses basic or bearer auth. The old code had no such protection — a client could potentially override gateway auth credentials via passthrough headers if Authorization was in `gateway.passthrough_headers`.

### Security improvements

Silent fallback when `db` is `None` — headers silently dropped (Medium)

All three functions use this guard:
```bash
  if request_headers and db is not None:
      # ... compute passthrough headers
```

If `db` is None, no passthrough headers are forwarded at all — including `X-Upstream-Authorization`. The old code at least forwarded explicitly configured `gateway.passthrough_headers` without needing a DB session.

While all three current call sites pass `db=db`, the parameter is `Optional[None]` by design "to avoid breaking other callers." If a future caller omits db, header forwarding silently degrades. Consider either:
  - Logging a warning when `db` is `None` and headers would have been forwarded
  - Or making `db` required since all current callers have it available

### Test Coverage Assessment

The tests mock `compute_passthrough_headers_cached` indirectly (by mocking `global_config_cache` and settings), but they don't verify that `X-Upstream-Authorization` actually gets renamed. Consider adding a test that:
  - Sets `X-Upstream-Authorization: Bearer token` in request headers
  - Uses a real (non-mocked) `compute_passthrough_headers_cached`
  - Asserts the outbound headers contain `Authorization: Bearer token`


Minor suggestion to add a warning log when `db` is `None` causes passthrough headers to be skipped, and consider one test using the real `compute_passthrough_headers_cached` to verify the rename end-to-end.
